newsitem.title: FRANCE: Parliament demands better quality water.
newsitem.headline: Parliament demands better quality water.

text.p: The European Parliament called on Wednesday for strict and uniform emission standards to improve water quality.
Despite 20 years of EU water quality laws, rivers and lakes across the continent have been steadily polluted by nitrates and pesticides draining off farmland.
Only 10 percent of EU water now meets good standards, according to the European Environment Agency.
"It's time to change policy and focus on prevention instead of fixing pollution limits," said Karl-Heinz Florenz, author of an environment committee report on water.
In approving a European Commission report (COM(96)0059) on water policy, the parliament demanded that EU farm policy should discourage farmers from excessive use of nitrates and fertilisers.

But the German Christian Democrat said he was concerned that the Commission would leave emission standards and controls to member states which would weaken efforts for a general improvement in quality.
Parliament called for EU-wide environmental quality objectives to be set for water and special measures to protect wetlands -- a sanctuary for wildlife.
Extraction of underground water must also be strictly controlled so as to maintain an ecological balance.
Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard said during a debate that the Commission could accept the parliament's amendments.
Bjerregaard noted that the Commission was preparing separate directives on drinking, bathing and undergound water reserves in order to secure supplies for the 21st century.
